linguistics.meaning: Lovers Lane — literally ‘my sweetheart’s little path’
linguistics.type: noun phrase (possessed NA + diminutive NI path)

morphemes.gloss: 1sg possessive prefix: ‘my’ — the same prefix in nikosis ‘my son’ and nimâmâ ‘my mother’
NA noun (animate, dependent stem): ‘sweetheart, dear, lover.’ Always appears with a possessive prefix; the bare stem does not surface alone.
NI noun stem: ‘road, path, trail’ — the same stem in mêskanaw ‘road, trail’
NI diminutive ending: ‘little, small’ — the inanimate-noun cousin of the animate ‑sis (cf. sîpîs ‘little river / creek’ from sîpiy ‘river’)
NI noun: ‘road, trail, path.’ The diminutive form mêskanâs ‘little path’ on the plaque comes from this stem.

relatedForms.note: Free-standing word for ‘road/trail.’ With the diminutive ‑âs it becomes mêskanâs ‘little path / trail.’
The plural form. The catalogue text ‘nicimosak méskanâs’ used this plural; the plaque uses singular ‘nicimos’ (one beloved, not many).

relatedForms.english: Path, trail, road (the diminutive used here)
relatedForms.note: ‘Little path’ — the affectionate scale of a single-track trail through the bush, perfect for a singletrack lover’s lane.

quickReference.note: Headword on the plaque. Singular nicimos (one beloved), with circumflex ê on mêskanâs.
1sg possessed form. The bare stem cimos is dependent; it does not appear alone.
Free NI noun. Diminutive: mêskanâs ‘little path / trail.’

quickReference.english: Little river / creek (showing the same ‑âs diminutive)
quickReference.note: From sîpiy ‘river’ + diminutive ‑(î)s. Same NI-diminutive pattern as mêskanâs.
Same dependent stem cimos with the 2sg possessive ki‑.

culturalStory.heading: About nicimos mêskanâs — My Sweetheart’s Little Path
body: Lovers Lane is the rare trail name where the English and the Cree mean almost exactly the same thing. The plaque is a red-on-white heart filled with three interlocking gear-discs, each carrying a piece of the syllabics ᓂᒋᒧᐢ ᒣᐢᑲᓈᐢ in white — when you read the gears in heart-shape order they spell the phrase. ‘nicimos mêskanâs’ runs across the top in plain SRO; ‘Lovers Lane’ runs across the bottom. Two of these heart plaques are mounted on the wall.

The Cree breaks into two short pieces. nicimos is the 1sg possessed form of ‑cimos ‘sweetheart, dear, lover’ — the dependent stem that always appears with a possessor prefix (nicimos ‘my sweetheart’, kicimos ‘your sweetheart’, ocimosa ‘his/her sweetheart (obviative)’). mêskanâs is the diminutive of mêskanaw ‘road, trail, path’: literally ‘little path.’ Together: ‘my sweetheart’s little path’ — the affectionate scale of a singletrack through the river-valley bush.

The trail itself is in the Central Edmonton (North) network, on ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory), near Government House just up the bank from the river. Trailforks describes it well: ‘single track that winds through tight overhanging bush creating a cool tunnel effect — rolls and flows well in both directions.’ It is a blue trail (also locally called ‘Groat Road Roller Coaster’ or ‘Monkey Trail’ in MTB vernacular) — the kind of soft, looping line that the Cree name dignifies as a path you’d take a sweetheart down.

notes: PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE: The plaque is carved with SRO 'nicimos mêskanâs' (singular nicimos, NOT plural nicimosak; circumflex ê on mêskanâs, NOT acute é). The current catalogue creeName 'nicimosak méskanâs' has both errors — it pluralises the sweetheart and uses a French acute é instead of the Cree circumflex ê. Coordinator should update catalogue creeName to 'nicimos mêskanâs'.

PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE (syllabics): Catalogue creeSyllabics 'ᓂᒋᒧᓴᐠ ᒣᐢᑲᓈᐢ' encodes the broken plural form (note ‑ᓴᐠ ‘‑sak’ at the end of nicimos). The plaque-correct syllabics is 'ᓂᒋᒧᐢ ᒣᐢᑲᓈᐢ'. Coordinator should update creeSyllabics accordingly.

There is a possible carving variant nîcimos (with circumflex on the first î; itwêwina headword form). The carved plaque appears to use plain 'nicimos' (no î diacritic) — this is the form chosen here. Some Plains Cree dictionaries write nîcimos with long î; both are widely attested and the plaque’s short-i spelling is acceptable.

Morpheme bracketing ni‑ + cimos | mêskan‑ + ‑âs is the structural reading. cimos is a dependent NA stem that never surfaces without a possessive prefix (so ni‑cimos ‘my sweetheart,’ ki‑cimos ‘your sweetheart,’ etc.). mêskanâs is the regular NI diminutive of mêskanaw with the ‑âs ending and final-vowel reduction (mêskanaw → mêskan‑ + ‑âs).
